definition: Precedence means the condition of being treated as more important than someone or something else — first place in importance or order.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word precedence. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know precedence should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: At the space agency, safety checks always take precedence over the launch schedule.
Preference is weaker: a preference is just a mild liking, while precedence is a real ranking that decides what comes first.
Supremacy is stronger: supremacy means total dominance over everything else, while precedence simply means ranking ahead in importance or order.

A priority is the thing a person or plan ranks first — you finish your top priority before anything else. Precedence names the relation itself: the state of coming ahead of something in importance or order, as when safety takes precedence over speed. A priority is what you rank first; precedence is the ranking.

Primacy is the settled condition of holding first place — scholars debate the primacy of one theory over another. It describes a standing status. Precedence is more transactional: it says which of two competing claims gets handled first, here and now, as when safety checks take precedence over a schedule.

Superiority means being higher or better than others in quality, strength, or status — a team can show clear superiority. It is about being above, not about going first. Precedence is strictly about order: what gets dealt with before what, regardless of which is better.

Notice the standard phrase 'take precedence over.'

Nearly always appears in the phrase 'take(s) precedence over.' Don't confuse it with precedent — a past example used as a guide for later decisions — which is a different word taught elsewhere in this unit.
